text:
sam: FYI onboarding weirdness with the new zephyr-lite (llama-ish -> gemma-ish) conversion. Seen a reproducible token alignment glitch when ZWNJ + combining diacritics appear in long contexts (~6k-12k).

sam: Repro steps I used:
```bash
./scripts/bench_longctx.sh --model zephyr-lite --quant int4 --prompt tests/longctx/zwnj-diacritic.txt --seed 42 --max-tokens 4096
```

sam: The quantized int4 runner shows coherent output for short prompts but for long windows there's token dropout / shifted continuation. Looks like sometimes the kv-cache entries are being applied to the wrong token index.

eva: can you paste a minimal diff of model outputs (fp16 vs int4) for the same prompt?

sam: pasted short excerpt below (trimmed). Note the continuation divergence at the highlighted place:
```diff
--- fp16.out
+++ int4.out
@@
 ...the patient placed the medication on the kitchen table, near the window.
-Then she added a note: 'Keep an eye on the child\u200c'
+Then she added a note: 'Keep an eye on the child'
 ...the story continued about how the girl and her friend...
```

sam: the fp16 preserved the ZWNJ (\u200c) inside the quoted phrase; int4 run appears to have normalized it away which shifts token IDs and kv offsets.

sam: I dug into the tokenizer logs — the converter step that maps byte offsets into token ids is using NFC normalization path in zephyr conversion, while our int4 conversion pipeline applied NFKC earlier. leads to mismatch.

kai: tl;dr: different unicode normalization between conversion/export and runtime tokenization -> token id sequence mismatch -> kvcache index misalignment when prefix caching is used.

margaret: does this only happen with ZWNJ or also with other zero-widths like ZWJ/U+FEFF?

sam: tested ZWJ and U+FEFF quickly — ZWJ behaves similarly but with lower freq; U+FEFF (BOM) less so. Combining diacritics (accent marks) also amplify because they change grapheme boundaries and tokenization heuristics.

benchbot: [benchmark run 8790012350] Summary: 1) int4 coherence score -6.2% vs fp16 on longctx zwnj suite; 2) token shift events detected: 24 across 100 runs; 3) median shift position: 3250 tokens.

jon: can we reproduce on a non-quantized int8 build to see if quantization amplifies or just exposes it?

sam: yes — int8 (and fp16) both have same normalization as runtime converter and don't show token dropout. int4 exporter had an extra NFKC step introduced in pr#4123 to coalesce presentation forms.

kai: action items I'd propose:
- revert pr#4123 for int4 export (short term)
- add a unit that verifies byte-offset -> token-id mapping is lossless for a set of ZW* and diacritic-heavy samples (tests/tokenization/roundtrip_zwnj.py)
- update kvcache to track original byte offsets alongside token indices so we can detect misaligns at runtime and fall back (graceful degrade).

margaret: +1 on test. Also add a golden prompt that reproduces. can you attach the failing prompt file?

sam: attached test prompt snippet (inline):
```
She wrote: "أكرهُ عندما يتعطلُ الهاتففي منتصفِ المحادثة، وخصوصاً عندما يَظهَرُ نصٌّ مركّبٌ with accents: éôà and a ZWJ
"
```

eva: i'm worried about adding byte-offsets to kvcache state — that'll change cache keys. Could we instead canonicalize at the tokenizer boundary and make sure export and runtime share the same normalizer?

sam: export/runtime canonicalization is ideal. short-term revert and add detection. medium-term do both: canonicalize + kvcache safety checks.

jon: what about a mitigation that maps uncommon zero-widths to a sentinel token pre-tokenization (e.g., <ZWNJ>) so they are preserved across pipelines?

kai: tried sentinel mapping in a local branch — it works for preserving identity but adds a token that some quantizers treat badly (outlier embedding vector, quantization scale mismatch). needs embedding recalibration.

margaret: For canary rollouts: do not enable prefix caching for zephyr-lite on Dedicated until we have the fix. patch in routing to disable kv prefix caching by model id tag 'zephyr-lite-v1' for now.

eva: can someone open a short RFC / blameless blurb with repro steps + bench numbers? I'll triage prioritization with product.

sam: i'll open the RFC now: https://redwood-internal/notes/zephyr-zwnj-token-aliasing-8790012345 (draft)

benchbot: [attached logs] /artifacts/8790012345/bench-stdout.log

jon: thanks. i'll take the exporter revert + unit tests (assigning to me).

kai: i'll sketch the kvcache offset-guard and a runtime detection that emits a warning and disables prefix caching on mismatch.

margaret: eva — can you block Dedicated canary for that model until next patch?

eva: done :white_check_mark: routing change queued.

sam: final note: this is a good example of how unicode normalization differences get amplified by quantization and caching. lemme know if you want more sample cases, i collected ~30 prompts in tests/longctx/zwnj-suite/ with multiple languages.

eva: great, thanks. ping when RFC is ready and when jon's revert PR is up so we can schedule a quick canary. :thumbsup:
